🔁 review — changes requested

Recorded by operator via the declared `review-pr` operation (#3035).

## Human review verdict — web-everything/web-everything#1559

**Verdict:** ✅ pass — no blocking findings

### Panel verdicts

| lens | weight | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| correctness | mandatory | accept |

### Findings (1)

**broken-reference** (1)
- `agent-memory-src/full-concurrency-is-the-default-never-a-cost-judgment.md:37` — The closing cross-reference `[[104-edit-work-runs-in-a-lane-clone]]` does not resolve to any file in the memory corpus. — An agent (or the `memory-resolve.mjs` tooling the corpus is built around) tries to open this pointer for the promised 'what disjoint has to mean' guidance and gets a hard miss. Confirmed by mutation probe: `node scripts/memory-resolve.mjs "104-edit-work-runs-in-a-lane-clone"` exits 2 with `no memory matches "104-edit-work-runs-in-a-lane-clone"`, while the sibling link on the same line, `node scripts/memory-resolve.mjs "shared-pool-lane-unsafe-for-manual-work"`, resolves cleanly to the real file. No test/gate reddens on this: `check-memory.mjs`'s pointer-integrity sweep only validates `](file.md)` markdown links and bare `- N.` index lines, never `[[slug]]` wikilinks inside a topic file's body, so the PR's reported '0 errors' is real but doesn't cover this reference. The same broken slug (`104-edit-work-runs-in-a-lane-clone`, vs. the actual file `104-feedback_commit_to_default_branch_ok.md`) already appears, equally unresolvable, in two pre-existing files (`pr-is-the-standard-flow-not-a-question.md`, `drain-gated-build-review-resolve-loop.md`) — this PR copies forward an existing broken pattern into a third, new location rather than originating the pattern. _[CONFIRMED]_ _[impact if unfixed: degraded]_
  - _Prevention (OWED — file it):_ Extend `check-memory.mjs`'s sweep to also scan every topic file's body for `[[slug]]` wikilinks and confirm each resolves via the same number-or-slug logic `memory-resolve.mjs` uses, flagging any miss as a violation — the sweep already does this for `](file.md)` links and `- N.` lines, just not for `[[...]]`.

---

**Decision:** `changes` — recorded by operator.
**Lens:** `correctness` — a SINGLE-LENS run. One `judge` step, one juror, one lens; the table above lists only the lens that judged. The other 3 panel lenses (security, simplicity, standards-conformance) did NOT run and are not reported as unjudged.
Net basis: `e9aa38f6eacb7ed0341cdcb4a191c5f9e56f0b15..3712d4bdcdf93206c53138a375bb615bfe02f541` (rev `origin/lane/memory-full-concurrency` at review time) — 2 net changed file(s) vs current main (#2450), not `gh pr diff`'s three-dot list.

_Recorded through the declared `review-pr` operation (#3035)._

## Independent reviewer — the blocking finding

The recorded write-up carries the juror's `correctness` finding (the broken `[[…]]` pointer, a carve-out).
That is **not** why this is `review:changes`. This is.

### HIGH — the rule contradicts the canonical panel doc, by name, without acknowledging it

The leaf's operative instruction is unqualified on cost and explicitly claims panels:

> "…do not reason about token or dollar cost at all. Applies to review spawns, prepare/build dispatches,
> **panels**, and lane work alike."
> "…ask ONLY *'does this share files, a lane, or another exclusive resource with something already
> running?'* If no → start it now, in parallel."

`we:docs/agent/build-ui.md:77` — the canonical home for panel sizing — says the opposite for that same case:

> "**Never climb a rung without asking the human first.** Escalation spends real budget and time, so it is
> their call, not a silent upgrade. And when there is **no operator channel to ask on** — an unattended
> `/workflow` lane, a conveyor run, a drain subagent — the answer is rung zero. Absence of an answer is a
> refusal, never a licence to proceed."

Its recall copy `agent-memory-src/right-size-the-panel-count-not-model-tier.md` — a **sibling in this same
`index-meta` category** — is equally explicit: *"a cost lever to earn, not a default … default to no panel,
ask before climbing a rung."*

**Why it's blocking, not cosmetic.** Extra panel seats on one question are disjoint by construction — no
shared file, no shared lane, no exclusive resource — so the leaf's scope test returns "no" and instructs the
agent to spawn them all, unasked. Two live rules in the same always-recalled category now give opposite
answers to the same question, and per `134-delegate-by-default…` *"if the two ever disagree, the doc wins"* —
so the leaf loses the disagreement it never declares. A memory rule's whole product is that it resolves at
recall time without interpretation; this one silently inverts an operator ruling. That is a regression in the
corpus, which is the one thing this PR ships.

**Note the shape of the error:** the leaf generalises from `delivery-loop.md` § *Parallelism and lane
hygiene* — which is about **lane tracks on disjoint files** — out to "panels", a case that section never
covers and that `build-ui.md` § *2. Mock before build* governs oppositely. A claim wider than its evidence.

**Fix (small):** carve the same-question case out — panel *seats* stay governed by
`[[right-size-the-panel-count-not-model-tier]]` / `build-ui.md` § 2 — and drop "panels" from the scope list,
or restate it as "independent work, **not** additional seats on one question". Add the `[[…]]` link so the
boundary is navigable, the way `134` already does for its neighbours.

---

### MEDIUM — the leaf's own point 2 overstates its evidence

> "2. **The stated reason was false.** Asked whether it was a file conflict, it was not…"

The stated reason *was* cost, and cost **was** the real reason — nothing about it was false. What actually
happened is what the PR body says correctly: *"The stated reason only surfaced when challenged."* The heading
claims a stronger fact than the body beneath it supports. In a rule about not substituting your judgment for
the operator's, the mislabel matters. Take the PR body's wording.

### LOW — the broken pointer (the juror's finding), with one correction

`[[104-edit-work-runs-in-a-lane-clone]]` does not resolve — `node scripts/memory-resolve.mjs
"104-edit-work-runs-in-a-lane-clone"` → `no memory matches`. Two pre-existing files carry the same broken
slug, so this PR copies the pattern forward rather than originating it. **Correction to the juror:** the bare
number *does* resolve — `memory-resolve.mjs 104` → `104-feedback_commit_to_default_branch_ok.md`, which is
topically right (it is the lane-clone rule). So only the name half is wrong. Cheap to fix in the same pass.

---

### What checked out

- **Home & shape** — `index-meta` is right (the sibling delegation/routing/panel rules live there); one leaf
  + one index line respects the tree; frontmatter and `**Why:** / **How to apply:**` match the convention.
- **No duplicate** — swept all 250 leaves by body and description; nothing already states this rule. The
  nearest neighbour is `right-size-the-panel…`, which is the *conflict* above, not a duplicate. The
  "update the existing file" clause does not apply.
- **The `delivery-loop.md` citation is accurate** — § *Parallelism and lane hygiene* does say run tracks
  concurrently on disjoint files, and *"wall-clock per track degrades while total throughput improves"* is
  verbatim. `[[shared-pool-lane-unsafe-for-manual-work]]` resolves.
- **Budget** — `check-memory.mjs`: index 3.3 KB / 25 lines / 250 topic files, within the 22 KB budget, ✓.
  The 200-char cap applies to the root `MEMORY.md` only, not sub-indexes; the new 321-char `index-meta` line
  is normal for that file (siblings run to 904).
- **Gate** — `npm run check:standards` in the foreground after a fresh `git fetch origin`, with the diff
  applied: **0 errors, 1435 warnings**. Claim confirmed exactly.

Reviewed independently in lane-18 against `origin/lane/memory-full-concurrency` @ `3712d4b`.

✅ review — accepted

## Human review verdict — web-everything/web-everything#1559

**Verdict:** ✅ pass — no blocking findings

### Panel verdicts

| lens | weight | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| correctness | mandatory | accept |

### Findings (1)

**broken-reference** (1)
- `agent-memory-src/full-concurrency-is-the-default-never-a-cost-judgment.md:45` — The closing line cites `[[104-edit-work-runs-in-a-lane-clone]]` as a place to see what "disjoint" must mean in this repo, but no such memory file exists. — Ran `node scripts/memory-resolve.mjs 104-edit-work-runs-in-a-lane-clone` (the repo's own resolver, per index-meta.md's usage line) directly against the current tree: it exits 2 with `no memory matches "104-edit-work-runs-in-a-lane-clone"`. The only file with a `104-` prefix in agent-memory-src is `104-feedback_commit_to_default_branch_ok.md`, about a different topic (committing to default branch), so numeric-prefix resolution also lands on the wrong file rather than the intended one. An agent following this rule's own pointer to learn what counts as scope-disjoint hits a dead link and gets nothing; the other two wikilinks in the same file ([[right-size-the-panel-count-not-model-tier]], [[shared-pool-lane-unsafe-for-manual-work]]) resolve fine, confirming this one specifically is broken rather than the syntax being unsupported. No test in scripts/__tests__/check-memory.test.mjs (or check-memory.mjs's sweep) validates wikilink targets — the sweep only checks markdown `](...)` links and `- N.` numeric references in index files, never `[[slug]]` references inside leaf-file prose — so this class of defect has no gate at all; no named test reddens. _[impact if unfixed: degraded]_
  - _Prevention (OWED — file it):_ Extend check-memory.mjs's sweep to also scan every topic file's prose for `[[slug]]` occurrences and validate each against the numbered/slug file set, the same way it already validates `](...)` links and `- N.` references — a small, deterministic addition to an existing gate.

**Decision:** `accept` — recorded by operator.
**Lens:** `correctness` — a SINGLE-LENS run. One `judge` step, one juror, one lens; the table above lists only the lens that judged. The other 3 panel lenses (security, simplicity, standards-conformance) did NOT run and are not reported as unjudged.
Net basis: `e9aa38f6eacb7ed0341cdcb4a191c5f9e56f0b15..ba1bcc1b24a8cebebe9e1bdd40d17d3d1322db70` (rev `origin/lane/memory-full-concurrency` at review time) — 2 net changed file(s) vs current main (#2450), not `gh pr diff`'s three-dot list.

## Independent reviewer — r2 accepted, with one carried-forward LOW

Reviewed independently against `origin/lane/memory-full-concurrency` @ `ba1bcc1b` (base `e9aa38f6` = current
`origin/main`, so no stale-base drift). Every citation below was opened, not taken on trust.

### r1's blocking findings — both genuinely fixed, in the diff, not in prose

**HIGH (panel contradiction) — FIXED.** `3712d4bd..ba1bcc1b` drops `panels` from line 32's scope list
(`Applies to review spawns, prepare/build dispatches, and lane work alike.`) and adds an explicit carve-out
at lines 34-39:

> "**This rule is about INDEPENDENT WORK — not about extra seats on ONE question…** Widening a panel, adding
> a second opinion on the same subject, or stacking jurors is governed by
> `[[right-size-the-panel-count-not-model-tier]]`: default zero, a rung to EARN, ask before climbing. Nothing
> here relaxes that."

Checked the target rule actually says that: `agent-memory-src/right-size-the-panel-count-not-model-tier.md` —
*"starting at zero… ask the human before climbing a rung"*, and `docs/agent/build-ui.md` § *2. Mock before
build* — *"Never climb a rung without asking the human first."* The characterisation is faithful, and
`node scripts/memory-resolve.mjs right-size-the-panel-count-not-model-tier` resolves. The two rules no longer
give opposite answers to the same question.

**MEDIUM (point 2 overstated its evidence) — FIXED.** Verbatim now:

> "2. **The real reason only surfaced when challenged.** … Cost *was* the actual reason; it just was not said
> until asked, and it had not been examined."

That is the PR body's own wording, which is what r1 asked for.

### LOW — NOT fixed, and knowingly so

`[[104-edit-work-runs-in-a-lane-clone]]` is still there at line 46. Re-confirmed against the PR corpus (diff
applied, so the new leaf is present): `node scripts/memory-resolve.mjs 104-edit-work-runs-in-a-lane-clone` →
`no memory matches`, while the sibling `[[shared-pool-lane-unsafe-for-manual-work]]` on the same line resolves.
The r2 commit message does not claim otherwise — it was simply left. r1 disposed it a carve-out and made the
HIGH the blocking reason, so it does not block this round either.

**Correction to the r2 juror, repeating r1's correction.** The juror says the numeric fallback "lands on the
wrong file… about a different topic (committing to default branch)". It does not. I read
`104-feedback_commit_to_default_branch_ok.md`: its description is *"Never branch in a shared checkout…; edits
land via a lane-clone -> ready-to-merge PR (#2183/#2190)"*, and its body is titled **SUPERSEDED in part** —
it IS the lane-clone rule, which is exactly the "what disjoint has to mean" guidance the pointer promises.
Only the name half of the slug is wrong; `memory-resolve.mjs 104` resolves to the topically-right file.

**Prevention still un-filed.** Both jurors set `preventionCaptured: false`; r1 marked it *OWED — file it*. I
swept `backlog/` for it — nothing exists (nearest neighbour is #2916, the 200-char sub-index budget, a
different gate). Extending `check-memory.mjs` to validate `[[slug]]` bodies is still owed as a card.

### What I re-verified myself

- **No gate covers this.** `grep -nE '\[\[' scripts/check-memory.mjs` → no hits. The sweep validates
  `](file.md)` links and `- N.` index lines only. So "0 errors" is true and simply does not cover wikilinks.
- **`delivery-loop.md` citation is accurate.** § *Parallelism and lane hygiene* (line 191): *"Run tracks
  concurrently only on **disjoint files**… wall-clock per track degrades while total throughput improves."*
  Verbatim.
- **Budget numbers are right, post-change.** `check-memory.mjs` with the diff applied: index 3.3 KB / 25 lines
  / **250** topic files, ✓ within 22 KB. On clean `main` it reports 249 — so the PR's "250" is the correct
  post-merge figure, not a copy of the baseline. New `index-meta` line is 321 chars; the 200-char cap in
  `check-memory.mjs` (`MAX_LINE`) applies to the root index only, and the gate passes.
- **Placement claim holds.** `index-meta.md` is where `134. Delegate By Default`, `workflow-lane-model-policy`
  and `right-size-the-panel…` already live. One leaf + one index line.
- **Gate, foreground, after `git fetch origin`, PR diff applied:** `npm run check:standards` →
  **0 error(s), 1435 warning(s)**. Claim confirmed exactly.

### One nit, non-blocking

Line 39's *"two jurors on the same PR are one piece of work and **the count is asked for**"* is imprecise for
jurors specifically: `docs/agent/jury-refinement-method.md` § *When to run the full jury* says the count is a
pure derivation (`panelRigorForCareLevel`) from the care band you pick — you don't ask the human for a juror
number. It errs safe (ask rather than silently spawn) and the routing pointer is correct, so it stays a nit.

---

**Verdict: `accept`.** Both blocking findings are fixed in the diff and verified against their sources; the
residual is a one-line dead pointer that already exists, unresolvable, in two other leaves and was carved out
last round. Recorded through the declared `review-pr` operation.
